## resultado
It applies schema migrations and request-log indexing, then exits (`litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py:1213`; https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/database_migrations.md). From v1.109.0, dry-run against a restored copy; dry runs take real table locks. An image rollback does not undo migrations.

## 5. Probes, drain, and rollout

`GET /health/liveliness` is unauthenticated and returns `"I'm alive!"` or 503 during shutdown; `GET /health/readiness` returns `{"status": "healthy", "db": ...}` and 503 when the database is unreachable (`litellm/proxy/health_endpoints/_health_endpoints.py:2440`, `:2333`; https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/health.md).

`SIGTERM` drains in-flight requests. From v1.108.0 the drain waits at most `GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` seconds (default 30), so raise it above your longest request and keep `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` above it. A 10-second `preStop` sleep lets ingress routing update; `maxUnavailable: 0` preserves capacity (https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/upgrade_guide.md). `/health/drain` is an optional hook: 404 unless `enable_drain_endpoint: true`, token-gated by `X-Drain-Token` (`litellm/proxy/health_endpoints/_health_endpoints.py:2392`). Add a startup probe because model loading can outlast the liveness delay (https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/high_throughput.md).

## 6. Image pinning and signing

Pin a release tag or digest. The chart leaves `image.tag` empty to inherit `appVersion` and appends `image.digest` as `repository:tag@digest` (`litellm/deploy/helm/litellm/values.yaml:33-37`). The quickstart compose uses `:latest` and is explicitly not a production pin (`litellm/deploy/docker/docker-compose.quickstart.yml:14`).

GHCR images are cosign-signed since v1.83.0. Verify first:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.6
```

The key is checked in at `cosign.pub:1-3`; the docs publish its fingerprint and a Sigstore policy example (https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/docker_image_security.md).

## 7. Secrets and exposure

Set `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` (must start with `sk-`) and `LITELLM_SALT_KEY` from a secret manager; `general_settings.master_key` overrides the variable, so avoid literals. Set `LITELLM_MODE=PRODUCTION` to disable `load_dotenv()`, and `trusted_proxy_ranges` to the ingress CIDRs so the UI login limiter sees real addresses (https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/prod.md).

The master key is the admin credential and UI password; rotating it signs everyone out. The salt key encrypts stored provider credentials and must not change after models are added (https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/master_key_rotations.md). Keep Postgres and Redis private.

## 8. Read-only root filesystem

The image runs as uid 65532 and supports `readOnlyRootFilesystem`; runtime writes belong under `/app/.cache`, `/var/lib/litellm`, and `/tmp` (`litellm/deploy/docker/README.md:62`). Compose proves it with `read_only: true`, `cap_drop: ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, and tmpfs (`litellm/deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml:42-49`). Mount emptyDirs and set `LITELLM_UI_PATH`, `LITELLM_ASSETS_PATH`, `LITELLM_MIGRATION_DIR`, `PRISMA_BINARY_CACHE_DIR`, and `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, or the proxy logs `Permission denied` (https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/prod.md).

## 9. Autoscaling

The chart defaults the gateway HPA to 1–10 replicas at 70% CPU and 80% memory, with KEDA as an alternative (`litellm/deploy/helm/litellm/values.yaml:494-495`; https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/deploy/helm.md). Scale on RPS and TPS too: CPU can stay idle while requests wait on providers. Set `minReplicas: 2` so a drain cannot take the last replica, and cap `maxReplicas` at the connection budget from §4.

## comando
```sh
cd /home/one/projects/one/ai-guides/tooling/litellm_guide && python3 - <<'EOF'
import re,os
files=['16-client-integration.md','17-production-deployment.md','18-operations-and-troubleshooting.md','19-upgrade-and-maintenance.md','20-decisions-and-pitfalls.md','21-quick-reference.md']
root='/tmp/litellm-src'; pat=re.compile(r'([A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.(?:py|sh|yml|yaml|prisma|pub|toml|json|md)):(\d+)(?:-(\d+))?')
for f in files:
    s=open(f).read(); body,src=s.split('## Sources',1)
    urls={u.rstrip('.,;') for u in re.findall(r'https://docs\.litellm\.ai/[^\s)`]+',body)}
    listed={u.rstrip('.,;') for u in re.findall(r'https://docs\.litellm\.ai/[^\s)`]+',src)}
    full=set(re.findall(r'[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.(?:py|sh|yml|yaml|prisma|pub|toml|json|md):\d+(?:-\d+)?',s))
    grouped=set()
    for line in s.splitlines():
        paths=re.findall(r'([A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.(?:py|sh|yml|yaml|prisma|pub|toml|json|md)):\d+(?:-\d+)?',line)
        if paths:
            for g in re.findall(r'`:(\d+(?:-\d+)?)`',line): grouped.add(f'{paths[-1]}:{g}')
    bad=[]
    for m in pat.finditer(s):
        p,a,b=m.group(1),int(m.group(2)),m.group(3); end=int(b) if b else a
        fp=os.path.join(root,p)
        if not os.path.isfile(fp): bad.append((p,a,'missing')); continue
        n=len(open(fp,errors='replace').read().splitlines())
        if not (1<=a<=end<=n): bad.append((p,a,b,n))
    last=[l for l in s.splitlines() if l.startswith('## ')][-1]
    print(f'{f}: {len(s.encode())}B cites={len(urls|full|grouped)} bad={bad} unused={listed-urls} missing={urls-listed} last={last}')
EOF
```
